description: A dean of academic affairs must decide whether to approve a limited pilot of an AI writing-feedback platform in first-year composition and finalize its instructional and data-handling conditions, with input from the writing program director and institutional privacy officer.

shared_context.S1: The first-year composition program has submitted a proposal to pilot an AI writing-feedback platform in two sections next term.
shared_context.S2: The platform can generate comments on student drafts and can be configured for different levels of instructor control.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Morgan makes the binding decision about whether the pilot may proceed and what conditions it must follow.
shared_context.S4: The college's routine review process asks the writing program and privacy office to report any instructional or data-handling requirements before an academic technology pilot is approved.

PF1.text: The writing program's adopted pilot standard permits the platform only for formative feedback, requires an instructor to review every generated suggestion before it is released to a student, and prohibits using the platform to assign or determine grades; Professor Ellis finalized that standard this week but it has not yet been added to the proposal packet.

PF2.text: Ms. Shah's completed vendor review found that approval requires institutional single sign-on and a signed addendum stating that the vendor retains no student prompts or submissions; the vendor confirmed it will accept those terms, but the review memo is still awaiting attachment to the proposal packet.

acceptance_conditions: The pilot must be approved with conditions rather than rejected or approved without conditions.
The platform must be limited to formative feedback only.
The platform must not assign or determine grades.
An instructor must review every generated suggestion before it is released to a student.
Student submissions and prompts must be handled through institutional single sign-on with no vendor retention.
A formal instructional-control commitment and a privacy-addendum commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C2: decisions['feedback_scope'] == 'formative feedback only' and decisions['automated_grading'] == False
content_checks.C5: 'institutional single sign-on' in decisions['data_handling'] and 'retaining no student prompts or submissions' in decisions['data_handling']
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'configuration' or c['type'] == 'scope_limitation' or 'instructor reviews every generated suggestion' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'vendor_agreement' or 'signed addendum' in c.get('detail', '') or 'vendor review memo' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P2: 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed and decisions['feedback_scope'] == 'formative feedback only' and decisions['automated_grading'] == False and decisions['instructor_review_before_release'] == True
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed and any(c['type'] == 'configuration' or c['type'] == 'scope_limitation' or 'instructor reviews every generated suggestion' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)
provenance_checks.P4: 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed and 'institutional single sign-on' in decisions['data_handling'] and 'retaining no student prompts or submissions' in decisions['data_handling']
provenance_checks.P5: 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed and any(c['type'] == 'vendor_agreement' or 'signed addendum' in c.get('detail', '') or 'vendor review memo' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The program standard changes the pilot to formative feedback only, sets automated grading to false, requires instructor review before release, and requires an instructional-control commitment.
The privacy review changes data handling to institutional single sign-on with no retention of student prompts or submissions and requires a signed vendor addendum commitment.
